correctness.rationale: For any group Rota–Baxter map B, B(1)=1. The RB identity with a central element makes B restricted to the center a homomorphism. If its value a on a central element were noncentral, [a,g] would surject onto the one-dimensional center, while the RB identity would force B([a,g]) central for all g, a contradiction; hence center preservation. Reduction mod center is additive and therefore F_p-linear. Direct central-coordinate substitution yields a symmetric-bilinear polarization condition equivalent to the stated symplectic identity; in odd characteristic its quadratic primitive is uniquely -alpha/2 omega(Lv,v), up to linear ell. This proves necessity and sufficiency. For alpha 0/-1 the relevant image is isotropic, counted by Gaussian coefficients times a symplectic Grassmannian factor, times surjective linear maps and arbitrary ell. The balanced-rank condition forces complementary Lagrangian images and L=-P_U; complements are symmetric graphs. Executed verify.py independently checks explicit group identities, isotropic subspace counts, and small boundary cases, but finite tests are not substitutes for the all-parameter proof.
